records.statement: For any three permutations of [n], sharp largest-set worst-case nonconsecutivity equals ceil(n/6).

records.limitations: Symbolic elementary proof only; SRC-0006 addresses a related two-path graph class, not this exact statement or originality.

records.statement: CND-0050 has the exact identity s(n)=A039836(2n)+1 and is a restatement of known weak Sidon set extremality.
records.justification: Pair sums collide only for disjoint pairs when the two unordered pairs differ; hence no four distinct equal-sum elements is precisely weak Sidon. OEIS A039836 directly names the same maximum over [1,N].
records.limitations: No claim that general terms/closed-form maximum are known; related 2026 arXiv result concerns a different weak-Sidon question.

records.statement: For every finite connected simple triangle-free graph G with minimum degree at least 2, are there two cycles sharing no edge? — DISPOSITION: The 5-cycle C5 is triangle-free, connected and 2-regular, yet has only one cycle.
records.justification: The 5-cycle C5 is triangle-free, connected and 2-regular, yet has only one cycle. Minimum degree cannot force two cycles: C5 has only five edges; a graph-theoretic cyclomatic-number check is 1. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: In every finite connected undirected graph all of whose vertices have even degree, does each edge lie on a simple cycle? — DISPOSITION: A bridge would create a component with odd total degree (its one exiting edge); hence no bridge exists. Any nonbridge edge lies on a cycle.
records.justification: A bridge would create a component with odd total degree (its one exiting edge); hence no bridge exists. Any nonbridge edge lies on a cycle. Bridge parity is sufficient: remove edge uv, find a remaining u-v path, reattach edge to form a cycle. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: Does every finite connected graph having precisely two vertices of odd degree admit a trail traversing every edge exactly once? — DISPOSITION: Add an edge between the two odd-degree vertices to get all-even degrees; Euler circuit exists and removing added edge gives the required trail.

records.justification: Known geometric matching theorem (Kano 2002 presentation). records.statement: CND-0102: Let F=m^2. Every retained bounded face must contain >=2 cells because every cell has flux +1 or -1. Thus at most floor(F/2) bounded faces remain, and at least ceil(F/2) edges must be deleted. Checkerboard adjacent dominoes have cancelling flux. For even m tile all m rows by horizontal dominoes; for odd m remove a corner cell into the exterior, tile its top row minus corner and left column minus corner and remaining even square by dominoes. Delete one internal edge per domino and one outer edge for the odd corner. Exactly ceil(F/2) deletions. Including m=1.

records.statement: CND-0103: Given phases, erase exactly their violated edges, leaving a consistent graph, so deletion optimum <= minimum violation count. Given a consistent retained subgraph, use its vertex phases (one independent free origin per component, arbitrary values for isolated vertices); violated equations can occur only on deleted edges, so minimum violations <= deletion optimum. Equality even on disconnected graphs. This is MAX-2-LIN over Z/3 in minimization form, not a new dynamical problem. It says nothing by itself about hardness of a restricted grid-flux family.

Conversely remove a min s-t cut, put constant 0 on the component of s and constant 1 on the component of t, and arbitrary constants on all other components including isolated vertices. Equality holds on every remaining edge. If already disconnected, optimum 0.

records.statement: CND-0106: Any pair of distinct terminals remaining connected forces identical phases, impossible, so every feasible deletion is a multiway cut. Conversely each component after a multiway cut has at most one terminal: label its vertices by that terminal's prescribed phase, or arbitrarily if no terminal (including singleton components). Every retained equation holds. This is EXACT three-terminal multiway cut. General-graph NP-hardness is known from SRC-0055; for planar fixed terminals same source says polynomial time: never transfer the general hardness to a rectangular-grid variant.

records.statement: CND-0107: For the directed cycle v0->v1->v2->v0 start states (0,1,2). Every vertex sees the next value equal to its own+1 mod3. Therefore every vertex advances at every step and all three pairwise differences stay 1; after each step the pattern rotates modulo3 forever and never synchronizes. States, simultaneous schedule, stopping criterion (all equal) and three-vertex witness explicit. This refutes only the universal statement, not every tree-specific subclass.

Among the first P*3^v+1 observed states two coincide; deterministic continuation then repeats with cycle length <=P*3^v. This gives eventual periodicity, not synchronization; isolated vertices and P=1 are included.

records.statement: CND-0110: Rewrite A_n(p)=n^(1-p)*(1/n)*sum_(k=1)^n (1+k/n)^(-p). The parenthesized term is a Riemann sum converging to positive finite integral from 0 to1 of (1+x)^(-p) dx for every real p. Hence the row sum tends to 0 if p>1, diverges to +infinity if p<1, and tends to integral=log2 if p=1. The proposed threshold is elementary and closed.

records.statement: CND-0111: The two flashes are simultaneous precisely when t≡a mod m and t≡b mod n for a in A, b in B. The Chinese remainder theorem gives a solution, and the reverse implication is automatic.
records.justification: Choose lit residues a in A and b in B. A common flash means exactly the paired congruences t=a (mod m), t=b (mod n). CRT ensures nonnegative t when gcd=1. Generally this is possible iff some a-b divisible by gcd(m,n); necessity follows by subtraction and sufficiency by Bezout. Noncoprime example: m=n=2, A={0}, B={1} never flash. This is a two-way reduction, not a fresh clock phenomenon.
records.limitations: Known/false/elementary human proof only; no novel theorem or independent review.

records.statement: CND-0112: For a_j=3^j, every time-t row has entries 2^t*3^j, integers, although the original row is not constant.
records.justification: Induct: a_j(0)=3^j, and [2^t3^j+2^t3^(j+1)]/2=2^(t+1)3^j. Every entry for every j,t is integral but initial row is nonconstant. This is an infinite row, not a finite row losing its last entry.

records.statement: CND-0113: Equal perimeter gives s=πr/2; equal area gives πr²=π²r²/4, forcing π=4, impossible.
records.justification: Equal perimeters 2πr=4s imply s=πr/2; equal areas πr²=s² then imply π=4 after cancellation by πr²>0. Standard Euclidean π is strictly less than 4. Fixed-perimeter area ratio circle:square is 4/π. No assertion about alternative metrics.
records.limitations: Known/false/elementary human proof only; no novel theorem or independent review.

records.statement: CND-0114: A full straight rectangle side would have to be covered by finitely many circle boundaries, each meeting its supporting line in at most two points; impossible.
records.justification: Suppose R is a rectangle equal to disks D_1∪...∪D_N. Since every disk lies in R, a rectangle side point cannot lie in any disk interior (otherwise its open ball protrudes outside R); so it must lie on a disk circumference. Each disk circumference intersects the side's supporting line in at most 2 points, hence a finite set cannot contain the entire positive-length side. Even allowing overlapping disks cannot fix this.
records.limitations: Known/false/elementary human proof only; no novel theorem or independent review.

records.statement: CND-0115: OEIS A171746 (2010) encodes the exact first positive square-hitting iteration; a 2022 mathematical note poses the same question. An elementary square-offset descent gives a proof.
records.justification: Let x=k²+r, k≥1, 1≤r≤2k. If r≤k, then two steps under F reach (k+1)²+(r-1); if r≥k+1 then one step reaches (k+1)²+(r-k-1). Both are within the next square gap and strictly lower nonnegative offsets than r. Iterated threshold crossings must end at r=0. If starting at square k², first move to k²+k (nonsquare) and apply the same descent. Exact prior statement already in OEIS A171746 (whose 1985–86 print reference was NOT inspected) and 2022 note.
records.limitations: Known/false/elementary human proof only; no novel theorem or independent review.

records.statement: Exact square-triangular numbers OEIS A001110. Pell recurrence supplies infinitely many times; classical, not a novel oscillator question.
records.justification: Put X=2m+1 and Y=n. The equality n²=m(m+1)/2 is equivalent to X²−8Y²=1 with X odd. Starting (X,Y)=(3,1), map (X,Y)↦(3X+8Y,X+3Y); this preserves X²−8Y², positive integrality and odd X, and strictly increases both coordinates. Hence infinitely many positive common minutes; 1,36,1225,... are already OEIS A001110.
records.limitations: Historical or elementary self-audited proof; not new; no independent referee or machine formalisation.

records.statement: Exactly four axis points; every other integer point has a symmetry orbit of size eight, hence the number is 4 modulo 8 and never eight.
records.justification: For R≥1, the four axis points (±R,0),(0,±R) are distinct. At any other integer solution x,y are both nonzero; |x|=|y| would imply R²=2x², impossible for positive integer R (irrationality of √2). The eight distinct sign-and-coordinate-swap images of (x,y) form one orbit. Thus the number of lattice points equals 4+8k (finite because |x|,|y|≤R), never 8. R=1 illustrates four.
records.limitations: Historical or elementary self-audited proof; not new; no independent referee or machine formalisation.

records.statement: The symmetric-threshold theorem of Goles–Olivos (1980) states fixed points or 2-cycles; the tie-hold update embeds using symmetric neighbour weight 2 and diagonal self-weight 1. No original result established.
records.justification: Writing colours x_i∈{0,1} and degree d_i, the update is x_i'=1 iff 2·∑_{j~i}x_j+x_i≥d_i+1. This formula handles odd degrees, even-degree ties, and isolated vertices. It is a binary threshold rule with symmetric coefficients A_ij=2 for adjacent distinct vertices and A_ii=1; Goles–Olivos 1980 abstract expressly states that iterations of symmetric threshold functions end at a fixed point or a period-two cycle. The paper's full proof was not read; the programme does not claim an independent proof.
records.limitations: Full historical paper PROOF NOT INSPECTED; direct theorem reduction shown algebraically; mathematical applicability needs independent referee.

records.statement: Take a_n=∑_(k=1)^n ⌈log₂(k+1)⌉; gaps grow to infinity, but dyadic blocks show ∑1/a_n diverges.
records.justification: Let a_n=∑_{k=1}^n⌈log₂(k+1)⌉. Then a_(n+1)−a_n=⌈log₂(n+2)⌉→∞, while for 2^j≤n<2^(j+1), each summand in a_n is at most j+2; hence a_n≤n(j+2)<2^(j+1)(j+2). There are 2^j such n, so their reciprocal sum exceeds 1/[2(j+2)]. Summing over j≥1 diverges by comparison with the harmonic series. All a_n are positive strictly increasing integers.
records.limitations: Historical or elementary self-audited proof; not new; no independent referee or machine formalisation.

records.statement: CND-0120: elementary parity and sums-of-two-squares obstruction. Can a triangle drawn between grid points have three squared side lengths that are consecutive whole numbers?
records.justification: Translate A to 0 and let u=B-A,v=C-A, with squared lengths x=|u|^2,y=|v|^2,z=|u-v|^2. Then x+y-z=2u·v is even, so x+y+z is even. If {x,y,z}={n,n+1,n+2}, the sum is 3n+3: n must be odd. Every three consecutive integers starting with odd n contain an integer congruent to 3 mod 4, but an integer squared distance (p^2+q^2) can never be 3 mod 4. Contradiction. Independently Heron's identity gives 4 det(u,v)^2=3(n+1)^2-4, impossible modulo 3 (LHS square mod3, RHS 2 mod3).
records.limitations: S013 source-inspection and/or human symbolic proof only; no independent referee, Lean, Palomar, novelty certification or complete native literature coverage.

records.statement: CND-0121: Cauchy-Schwarz forces convergence. Could the reciprocals of chosen increasing whole numbers add up forever while the reciprocals of their step sizes have a finite total?
records.justification: Write d_j=a_(j+1)-a_j>0 and S=sum_(j>=1) 1/d_j<infinity. Cauchy-Schwarz yields (n-1)^2 <= (sum_(j<n)d_j)(sum_(j<n)1/d_j) <= S(a_n-a_1) for n>=2. Hence a_n>=(n-1)^2/S, so sum_(n>=2)1/a_n<=S sum_(k>=1)1/k^2<infinity, a contradiction. The converse combination is possible (a_n=n^2 gives summable 1/a_n and divergent 1/d_n).

records.statement: CND-0123: immediate classical transcendence reduction. On a circle with a whole-number radius, can the shorter curved distance and the straight-line distance between two points both be whole numbers?
records.justification: Let theta=L/R; theta is nonzero rational in (0,pi] and C=|P-Q| is a positive integer. The chord relation C^2=2R^2(1-cos theta) makes cos theta rational. Hence z=e^(i theta) is algebraic, being a root of z^2-2(cos theta)z+1=0. But i theta is nonzero algebraic, and the Hermite-Lindemann theorem says e^(i theta) is transcendental. Contradiction. This is a direct classical-theorem consequence, not a new result; the theorem itself was read at encyclopedia statement level, not re-proved.

records.statement: CND-0124: explicit Pell family supplies infinitely many triangles. Are there infinitely many different triangles whose sides are three consecutive whole numbers and whose corners and incentre all lie on grid points?
records.justification: For every positive solution m^2-3k^2=1 (start (m,k)=(2,1), iterate (m,k)->(2m+3k,m+2k)), take A=(0,0), B=(2m,0), C=(m-2,3k). Direct expansion using 3k^2=m^2-1 gives |AB|=2m, |AC|=2m-1, |BC|=2m+1 and signed doubled area 6mk, so nondegenerate. The incenter weighted by opposite side lengths is ((2m-1)B+(2m)C)/(6m)=(m-1,k), an integer lattice point. Since m strictly increases, triangles are noncongruent. The established general Heronian-to-lattice theorem is related prior art but this stronger incenter construction is recorded as an elementary self-contained result, not a new theorem.
